It solves the difficulty of mapping irregular unstructured grid data efficiently to GPU hardware by replacing the grid with a pixelized projection plane and 1D scalar functions (linear splines) defined on sampling rays [S1, S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the method solves the difficulty of mapping irregular unstructured grid data to GPU hardware by replacing the grid with a pixelized projection plane and 1D scalar functions (linear splines) defined on sampling rays. The evidence in Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly describes the 'PRI' (Pixelized Ray Integral) representation. It details how the PRI uses a 'pixel plane' (index texture with same resolution as PRI pixel plane) and 'per-pixel splines' (linear splines) stored in a 'knots texture'. The text confirms that these splines are associated with pixels in the sampling plane (sampling rays) and are used to represent the unstructured grid data efficiently for rendering on GPU hardware (via textures). Therefore, every fact in the claim is supported by the evidence.
